senses.title: Of land and its ownership
senses.definition: relating to land as property, especially to who owns and who works it
senses.definitionCN: 与作为财产的土地有关，尤其涉及谁拥有、谁耕作
senses.example: Land disputes in the valley are settled by agrarian law that dates back centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河谷的土地纠纷依数百年前传下的土地法解决。
senses.why: the word comes from the Latin word for field, so its core is land as an object held and divided.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示田地的词，因此其核心是作为被占有、被分割之物的土地。

senses.title: Of farming as a way of life
senses.titleCN: 作为一种生活方式的农耕
senses.definition: relating to the practice and rhythm of cultivating the soil
senses.definitionCN: 与耕作土地的实践和节奏有关
senses.example: The museum records the agrarian year from ploughing to threshing.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆记录了从犁地到脱粒的农事一年。
senses.why: owning land and working it are two sides of the same order, so the adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 拥有土地与耕作土地是同一秩序的两面，因此这个形容词两者都涵盖。

senses.title: Of land redistribution
senses.definition: used of reforms that change who holds land, often breaking up large estates
senses.definitionCN: 用于改变土地持有者的改革，常拆散大庄园
senses.example: Agrarian reform gave tenants title to the fields they farmed.
senses.exampleCN: 土地改革把佃农所耕田地的产权给了他们。
senses.why: if land is the basis of power, then changing its ownership is the central political demand of the word.
senses.whyCN: 如果土地是权力基础，那么改变其所有权就是这个词的核心政治诉求。

senses.title: Of a rural social order
senses.titleCN: 农村社会秩序意义上的
senses.definition: describing societies or economies organized around land, villages and rural classes
senses.definitionCN: 描述围绕土地、村落与农村阶级组织起来的社会或经济
senses.example: The region remained agrarian long after the coast industrialized.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海工业化很久之后，这个地区仍以农业为主。
senses.why: the adjective can describe a whole order, not only a single plot or law.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以描述整个秩序，而不只是单块土地或单条法律。

senses.title: A land-reform advocate
senses.definition: a person who campaigns for a fairer distribution of land
senses.definitionCN: 为更公平的土地分配而奔走的人
senses.example: The agrarian spoke at every village meeting that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天，这位土地改革者在每次村会上发言。
senses.why: the adjective became a noun for the person who carries its political programme.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转为名词，指承载其政治纲领的人。

senses.title: Roman land law
senses.definition: the body of ancient Roman laws about the division and use of public land
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马关于公地分配与使用的法律体系
senses.example: The agrarian laws limited how much public land one family could hold.
senses.exampleCN: 土地法限制一个家庭能占有的公地上限。
senses.why: the phrase is fixed in Roman history, where land division was a standing political conflict.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法在罗马史中固定下来，因为土地分配是长期的政治冲突。

senses.title: Of a farmed landscape
senses.definition: describing a landscape or ecology shaped by centuries of cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 描述被数百年耕作塑造的景观或生态
senses.example: The agrarian landscape of hedges and terraces supports many species.
senses.exampleCN: 由树篱与梯田构成的农耕景观养活了众多物种。
senses.why: land that has been worked for generations becomes a visible pattern, and the adjective names that pattern.
senses.whyCN: 被世代耕作的土地会成为可见的图案，这个形容词命名那种图案。

senses.title: Of rural unrest
senses.definition: describing conflict or crisis rooted in land hunger and tenure
senses.definitionCN: 描述源于土地饥渴与占有关系的冲突或危机
senses.example: The agrarian crisis drove thousands off the land and into the cities.
senses.exampleCN: 农业危机把成千上万人赶离土地、涌入城市。
senses.why: when tenure is unjust or unviable, the same word shifts from description to the name of a crisis.
senses.whyCN: 当土地占有不公或难以为继时，同一个词便从描述转为危机之名。

intro.en: Agrarian comes from Latin agrarius 'of land', built on ager 'field'. English adopted it in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: agrarian 来自拉丁 agrarius「土地的」，由 ager「田地」构成。英语在 16 世纪吸收这个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ager meant 'field, farmland, territory'. It also gives acre; its Indo-European source is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: ager 意为「田地、耕地、领地」，也构成 acre；其印欧来源属重构形式，而非有据可查的材料。

items.en: Agrarius meant 'of fields, relating to land', and was used of laws about public land and of the men who proposed them.
items.cn: agrarius 意为「田地的、与土地有关的」，用于关于公地的法律，也用于提出这些法律的人。

items.en: The leges agrariae of the Roman republic divided public land and limited holdings, which fixed the political sense of the word.
items.cn: 罗马共和国的土地法分配公地并限制占有上限，这固定了这个词的政治含义。

items.en: English took agrarian in the sixteenth century for matters of land and tenure, and later widened it to whole rural orders.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪吸收 agrarian，用于土地与占有事务，后来扩大到整个农村秩序。

items.en: Nineteenth-century land reform movements made the word a programme as well as a description, and its noun named the advocate.
items.cn: 19 世纪的土地改革运动使这个词既是描述也是纲领，其名词形式则指主张者。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin root of ager is a reconstruction, and the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：ager 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the land-family words that are most often confused; group two holds near neighbours of rural life.
note.cn: 第一组是最易混淆的土地词族成员；第二组是农村生活的近邻说法。

entries.definition: Of farming technique and production; it describes how food is grown, while agrarian describes land tenure and the rural order.
entries.definitionCN: 指农耕技术与生产；描述粮食如何种植，而土地一词描述土地占有与农村秩序。

entries.definition: The science of crop production and soil management; a technical field, not a social order.
entries.definitionCN: 作物生产与土壤管理的科学；属技术领域，不是社会秩序。

entries.definition: A unit of land area; it descends from the same word for field but names a measure, not a social question.
entries.definitionCN: 土地面积单位；与田地一词同源，但指度量，不指社会问题。

entries.definition: To convert land or a community to small-scale farming; rare and technical, unlike the everyday adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地或社群转为小农耕种；罕用且技术化，不同于日常形容词。

entries.definition: Of the countryside; it describes location and population density rather than land ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 乡村的；描述地点与人口密度，而非土地占有。

entries.definition: Of shepherds and grazing, and also of an idealized country life; it is not about crops or tenure.
entries.definitionCN: 牧人与放牧的，也指理想化的乡野生活；与作物或土地占有无关。

entries.definition: Describing people or families that own substantial land; it names the proprietor rather than the order.
entries.definitionCN: 描述拥有大量土地的人或家族；命名的是所有者而非秩序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means field, so agrarian is about land before it is about crops.
normal.cn: 词根意为田地，因此土地先于作物。

normal.en: Agrarian reform is the fixed phrase that shows the political sense.
normal.cn: 土地改革这一固定搭配展示了政治义。

normal.en: The pair agrarian and agricultural divides ownership from technique.
normal.cn: 土地的一词与农业的一词，把占有与技术分开。

normal.en: Roman agrarian laws are the historical anchor of the word.
normal.cn: 罗马土地法是这个词的历史锚点。

normal.en: As a noun it names the person who campaigns for land reform.
normal.cn: 作名词时，它指为土地改革奔走的人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plot of ground: land as property, farming as a way of life, redistribution, the rural order, the advocate, Roman land law, the farmed landscape and the unrest that tenure can cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一块地面展开：作为财产的土地、作为生活方式的农耕、土地再分配、农村秩序、主张改革的人、罗马土地法、被耕作塑造的景观，以及占有关系可能引发的动荡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deed, a plough, a boundary stone and a bag of seed on one table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌上放着地契、犁、界石与一袋谷种。

branches.en: PROPERTY: the base sense, land as something owned and divided.
branches.cn: 财产：基础义，作为被占有、被分割之物的土地。

branches.en: WORK AND LANDSCAPE: cultivation as a way of life, and the visible pattern it leaves.
branches.cn: 劳作与景观：作为生活方式的耕作，以及它留下的可见图案。

branches.en: REDISTRIBUTION: reform as a programme, and the advocate who carries it.
branches.cn: 再分配：作为纲领的改革，以及承载它的主张者。

branches.en: ORDER AND LAW: the rural order in general, and the Roman laws that fixed the term.
branches.cn: 秩序与法律：一般的农村秩序，以及固定这个术语的罗马法律。

branches.en: CONFLICT: when tenure fails, the same adjective names a crisis.
branches.cn: 冲突：当占有关系难以为继，同一个形容词成为危机之名。

intro.en: Agrarian is a Latin root plus an adjective suffix, and the root also yields agriculture and acre.

latinIntro.en: Latin ager 'field' gives agrarius and agrarian, and through cultura it also gives agriculture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ager「田地」给出 agrarius 与 agrarian，并经 cultura 给出 agriculture。

definition_zh: 协议；协定；一致；同意；（语法）一致关系
definition_en: a formal arrangement between people or groups, the state of sharing the same opinion, or the matching of grammatical forms
core_image: 两份文件并排放着，落款处是两个不同的签名，内容却完全相同
scene: 会议室里两支笔几乎同时落在一份文件上。Both companies signed the agreement on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 agreement 是「协议、协定」（第 1 个义项：双方正式达成的书面约定）；句意为两家公司在周五签署了这份协议。图中可辨识物件：文件、两支笔、会议桌。

pos.zh: 名词：协议；协定；一致；同意；（语法）一致关系

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「同意；商定」
由 agree 加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「分歧；争执」
由否定前缀加 agree 构成，义为「不同意」

senses.title: A formal arrangement
senses.definition: a formal arrangement or contract reached between two or more parties
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方正式达成的安排或合同
senses.example: Both companies signed the agreement on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司在周五签署了这份协议。
senses.why: The -ment suffix turns the act of agreeing into its result, so the word names the settled thing that both sides can sign.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ment 把「同意」这个动作转成动作的结果，因此这个词指的就是双方可以签字的那份定下来的东西。

senses.title: The state of sharing a view
senses.definition: the state of having the same opinion, or the fact of people sharing a view
senses.definitionCN: 持有相同意见的状态，或人们看法相同这一事实
senses.example: There is broad agreement that the rule needs changing.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍认为这条规定需要修改。
senses.why: This is the abstract side of the same suffix: not the signed document but the shared mind behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一词尾的抽象一面：不是签好的文件，而是文件背后那个相同的心思。

senses.title: Matching forms in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, the matching of a verb with its subject, or of an adjective with its noun
senses.definitionCN: 语法上动词与主语、形容词与名词之间的形式对应
senses.example: Subject-verb agreement is tested in the first section.
senses.exampleCN: 主谓一致在第一部分考查。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the everyday sense of 'falling into line' to describe forms that must match each other.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借用了日常义里「对齐」的意思，用来描述必须彼此对应的形式。

intro.en: Agreement is agree plus the French noun ending -ment, so it names both the act of agreeing and the thing agreed.
intro.cn: agreement 是 agree 加上法语名词词尾 -ment，既指「同意」这个动作，也指同意之后定下来的东西。

items.en: The root gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome', the source of agree and of gratitude.
items.cn: 词根 gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的」，是 agree 与 gratitude 的来源。

items.en: Agreer meant 'to please' and 'to consent'; its noun agrement named the consent itself.
items.cn: agreer 意为「使愉快」与「应允」；其名词 agrement 指应允这件事。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fifteenth century, and the spelling settled as agreement later.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，拼写后来才固定为 agreement。

items.en: The legal sense 'a binding arrangement' develops first, with the abstract sense 'shared opinion' alongside it.
items.cn: 「有约束力的约定」这一法律义先发展出来，「共同看法」这一抽象义同时存在。

items.en: The grammatical sense is added in the nineteenth century, when English grammar writing turned to Latin models.
items.cn: 语法义在十九世纪加入，当时英语语法写作正大量借用拉丁语法模型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agree family; the near-meaning group gathers documents and states of accord that differ in formality.
note.cn: 形近组收 agree 词族；近义组收表示「约定」的文件与「一致」状态，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to share an opinion or consent.
entries.definitionCN: 表示意见相同或应允的动词。

entries.definition: Pleasant, or willing to go along with something.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的，或乐意配合的。

entries.definition: A failure to agree, or a quarrel about it.
entries.definitionCN: 未能达成一致，或由此产生的争执。

entries.definition: A legally binding written arrangement between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间具有法律约束力的书面约定。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between states, usually signed and ratified.
entries.definitionCN: 国家之间的正式协议，通常需签署并批准。

entries.definition: A general agreement reached by a group as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体整体达成的普遍共识。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the verb agree and the French noun ending -ment.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：动词 agree 与法语名词词尾 -ment。

normal.en: Agreement is agree plus -ment: the suffix turns the act into the thing.
normal.cn: agreement 是 agree 加 -ment：词尾把动作变成那个东西。

normal.en: You sign an agreement but you are in agreement; one is a document, the other a state.
normal.cn: 你签署一份协议，但你是「处于一致之中」；一个是文件，一个是状态。

normal.en: Spell it with -ment, not -mant: the vowel before the ending is e, as in agree.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -ment 不是 -mant：结尾前的元音是 e，跟 agree 一致。

normal.en: Subject-verb agreement is just two forms falling into line, the same image as two parties.
normal.cn: 主谓一致不过是两个形式对齐，和双方达成一致是同一幅画面。

normal.en: A verbal agreement is still an agreement, though nothing is written down.
normal.cn: 口头协议仍是协议，只是没有写在纸上。

abstract.en: An agreement is a promise made durable: the shared mind is fixed in a form that outlasts the conversation.
abstract.cn: 协议是让承诺变得耐久：共同的心思被固定成一种比谈话活得更久的形式。

abstract.en: The same word covers a contract and a mood, because both are ways of things lining up.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指合同又指气氛，因为两者都是事物对齐的方式。

abstract.en: Grammar's use of agreement shows how deeply the idea of matching runs in language about language.
abstract.cn: 语法里也用 agreement，说明「彼此对应」这个观念在谈论语言时扎得多深。

examples.en: Both companies signed the agreement on Friday.
examples.cn: 两家公司在周五签署了这份协议。

examples.en: There is broad agreement that the rule needs changing.
examples.cn: 人们普遍认为这条规定需要修改。

examples.en: The teacher marked every agreement error in the essay.
examples.cn: 老师标出了文章中每一处一致关系错误。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses come from one act of lining up: a signed result, a shared mind, and grammatical forms that must match.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都来自同一个「对齐」的动作：签下来的结果、共同的心思，以及必须彼此对应的语法形式。

intro.en: The verb agree, the French noun ending -ment, and the negative prefix that reverses it.
intro.cn: 动词 agree、法语名词词尾 -ment，以及把意思反转的否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the root gratus is Latin; the noun itself was formed in French.
latinIntro.cn: 只有词根 gratus 属拉丁语，名词本身是在法语中构成的。

definition_zh: 小病；轻微疾病；不适
definition_en: an illness, especially a mild or chronic one that is not seriously dangerous
core_image: 一件贴身的小毛病，像口袋里揣了太久的小石子
scene: 诊所的候诊室里坐满了老人，护士轻声叫号。The doctor treated every minor ailment with patience.
sceneCN: 这里的 ailment 是「小病、不适」（第 1 个义项：不太严重的疾病）；句意是医生耐心诊治每一种小毛病。

pos.zh: 小病；轻微疾病；慢性不适

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「使苦恼；使患病」
加现在分词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「生病的；境况不佳的」

senses.title: A mild illness
senses.definition: an illness, especially one that is mild or long-standing rather than life-threatening
senses.definitionCN: 一种疾病，尤指不严重或长期缠身而非危及生命的病
senses.example: The doctor treated every minor ailment with patience.
senses.exampleCN: 医生耐心地诊治每一种小毛病。
senses.why: The verb ail means to trouble; the noun names the trouble itself, small and persistent like a stone in the pocket.
senses.whyCN: 动词 ail 意为「使苦恼」；名词指的就是这种苦恼本身，小而缠人，像口袋里的石子。

senses.title: A chronic bodily or mental disorder
senses.definition: a disorder of body or mind that keeps troubling someone over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期困扰人的身体或心理失调
senses.example: Modern medicine has remedies for most age-related ailments.
senses.exampleCN: 现代医学对大多数与年龄相关的病痛都有对策。
senses.why: Because the root image is ongoing trouble rather than sudden harm, the word fits conditions that linger rather than strike.
senses.whyCN: 因为词根意象是「持续的困扰」而非突然的伤害，所以这个词适合形容缠绵不去的病况。

intro.en: From a verb meaning to trouble, first the body, then the spirit.
intro.cn: 来自一个表示「使苦恼」的动词，先指身体，后指心灵。

items.en: eglan meant to trouble or afflict, related to egle, troublesome, painful.
items.cn: 古英语 eglan 意为「使苦恼、折磨」，与 egle（麻烦的、痛苦的）同源。

items.en: The verb ailen meant to trouble or afflict, used of bodies and of hearts alike.
items.cn: 中古英语动词 ailen 意为「使苦恼」，既用于身体也用于心灵。

items.en: The noun suffix -ment turned the verb into a thing: the trouble itself, an ailment.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ment 把动词变成一件事物：苦恼本身，即一种小病。

items.en: The noun appears in English in the fifteenth century, first of bodily complaints.
items.cn: 该名词于十五世纪见于英语文献，最初指身体上的病症。

items.en: Modern English keeps ailment for mild or chronic complaints, while ailing describes a person or business in poor shape.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ailment 指轻微或慢性的病痛，ailing 则形容身体不佳或经营不善的人或机构。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike kin of the verb ail; the second collects nouns for illness of different weights.
note.cn: 第一组收动词 ail 的形近同族词；第二组收集表示不同轻重疾病的名词。

entries.definition: to trouble or affict someone in body or mind; mostly used in questions like what ails you
entries.definitionCN: 使苦恼；使患病；多用于 what ails you 这类问句

entries.definition: in poor health, or (of a business) struggling
entries.definitionCN: 生病的；（企业等）境况不佳的

entries.definition: a beer-like drink; only similar in sound, not related in origin
entries.definitionCN: 麦芽酒；只是发音相近，词源无关

entries.definition: an illness, especially one reported to a doctor
entries.definitionCN: 疾病；尤指向医生述说的病症

entries.definition: an illness, often a serious or widespread one, sometimes figurative
entries.definitionCN: 疾病；常指严重或流行之病，也可作比喻

entries.definition: a disruption of normal physical or mental function
entries.definitionCN: （身心机能的）紊乱；失调

entries.definition: something that causes pain or suffering, including illness
entries.definitionCN: 痛苦；折磨；也包括病痛

normalIntro.en: ail (trouble) plus -ment (a thing): the thing that troubles you.
normalIntro.cn: ail（使苦恼）加 -ment（表示事物）：那个让你难受的小东西。

normal.en: ailment is the noun form of the verb ail, meaning a minor illness.
normal.cn: ailment 是动词 ail 的名词形式，指小病。

normal.en: -ment builds nouns from verbs, as in treatment and movement.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成名词，如 treatment、movement。

normal.en: Ailing describes someone in poor health; ailing companies are also said to be sick.
normal.cn: ailing 形容健康不佳；经营不善的公司也说 ailing。

normal.en: Common collocations: a minor ailment, a chronic ailment, age-related ailments.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：a minor ailment、a chronic ailment、age-related ailments。

normal.en: What ails you? asks what troubles you — the ailment is the answer.
normal.cn: What ails you?（你哪里不舒服？）—— ailment 就是那个答案。

abstract.en: Picture a small pebble carried in a shoe: it never stops the journey, but it always nags.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里的一颗小石子：不挡路，却一直硌脚。

abstract.en: See a shelf of small jars in a country pharmacy, each labelled with a small trouble.
abstract.cn: 想象乡村药铺的一排小药罐，每个罐子上都贴着一种小毛病。

abstract.en: Imagine an old man opening his coat to show not one great wound but many small aches.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老人敞开外衣，里面不是一处大伤，而是许多小小的疼痛。

examples.en: She visited the clinic for a minor ailment.
examples.cn: 她因为一点小病去了诊所。

examples.en: Cold remedies are sold for every common ailment.
examples.cn: 治各种常见小病的药都有出售。

examples.en: Her ailments multiplied as she grew older.
examples.cn: 她上了年纪，病痛也多了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿闷」——爱儿闷闷不乐，原来是有点小毛病。

root: 源自古英语 eglan「使苦恼」，中古英语动词 ail 保留此义，加名词后缀 -ment 后指「苦恼之事」，即小病、不适。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses grow from one image: a trouble that persists without becoming grave.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都源于同一意象：一种持续存在却不算严重的困扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small persistent trouble, a pebble in the pocket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个持续的小困扰，像揣在口袋里的石子。

branches.en: The pebble becomes a mild illness that a doctor can name and treat.
branches.cn: 小石子变成一种医生能命名、能治疗的轻微疾病。

branches.en: The pebble stays in the pocket for years: the complaint turns chronic.
branches.cn: 小石子常年留在口袋里：病症转为慢性。

branches.en: The collection of pebbles weighs on the whole person: decline sets in.
branches.cn: 石子越积越多，压垮整个人：衰弱由此开始。

branches.en: The same trouble can sit in the mind: weariness and low spirits.
branches.cn: 同样的困扰也可以落在心里：倦怠与低落。

branches.en: Figuratively, even a sick organization can be said to suffer ailments.
branches.cn: 作比喻时，连不景气的机构也可以说患了「病痛」。

intro.en: A native English root plus a Latin-built noun suffix: one short word, two traditions.
intro.cn: 一个本土英语词根加一个源自拉丁的名词后缀：短短一词，两大传统。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -ment came through French from Latin menta; it builds nouns of action or result.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -ment 经法语来自拉丁语 menta，用于构成表示动作或结果的名词。

items.meaning: the result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作的结果或手段

items.meaning: the act or manner of treating
a reason given for or against something
an illness; an expression of dissatisfaction

items.example: the root of eglan, to trouble

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「使苦恼；使患病」
加现在分词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「生病的；境况不佳的」

definition_zh: 通风的；宽敞明亮的；轻快的；不切实际的
definition_en: full of fresh air, light and spacious, cheerful and light in manner, or lacking substance
core_image: 开满窗的白色房间：风穿过，光线也穿过，什么都留不住
scene: 她推开门，海风一下子灌满了整个房间。The studio has an airy loft with tall windows on every side.
sceneCN: 这里 airy 是「通风的、宽敞明亮的」（第 1 个义项：空气流通、光线充足）；句意是工作室的阁楼四面高窗，明亮通透。

pos.zh: 通风的；明亮的；轻快的；空洞的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「空气；神态」；airy 由其加 -y 构成
airy 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「轻快地；漫不经心地」
airy 加 -ness，义为「通风；轻盈；空洞」

senses.title: Full of fresh air and light
senses.definition: having plenty of fresh air moving through, and feeling open and light
senses.definitionCN: 空气流通、光线充足，令人感觉开阔轻盈
senses.example: The kitchen is airy, with windows on two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这间厨房两面开窗，通风明亮。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns air into a quality; a room with air moving through it is literally 'full of air'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 把 air 变成一种性质；空气流通的房间就是字面上的「满是空气」。

senses.title: Cheerful and casual in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a light, easy, and unconcerned way
senses.definitionCN: 举止轻松随意、若无其事
senses.example: She gave an airy wave and walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻快地挥了挥手，继续往前走。
senses.why: Air is weightless, so a person acting 'like air' moves lightly and lets nothing weigh on them.
senses.whyCN: 空气没有重量，举止「像空气一样」的人便步履轻盈、百事不萦怀。

senses.title: Lacking substance or detail
senses.definition: not based on facts or solid plans; vague and unrealistic
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏事实或切实计划支撑的；含糊而不现实的
senses.example: The candidate offered airy promises instead of a plan.
senses.exampleCN: 候选人只给了空洞的承诺，拿不出方案。
senses.why: What is made of air has no weight and cannot be held, so airy ideas are ones you cannot grasp.
senses.whyCN: 空气做的东西没有分量也抓不住，因此 airy 的想法就是无法落实的想法。

intro.en: A simple English compound: the noun air plus the adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: 简单的英语复合词：名词 air 加形容词后缀 -y。

items.en: aer meant the lower air, the layer human beings breathe.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指低层大气，即人呼吸的空气。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as aer, keeping the sense of air and atmosphere.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 aer，仍指空气、大气。

items.en: Old French air passed the word on to English with its Greek-Latin pedigree intact.
items.cn: 古法语 air 把这个词连同希腊-拉丁血统一并传给英语。

items.en: air entered English in the sense of the atmosphere we breathe.
items.cn: 14 世纪 air 进入英语，指我们呼吸的大气。

items.en: airy was formed with -y, first describing open, well-ventilated places.
items.cn: 16 世纪加 -y 构成 airy，最初形容开阔通风之处。

items.en: The word widened to light manners and empty, insubstantial ideas.
items.cn: 词义扩大到轻快的举止与空洞的想法。

note.en: The first group collects look-alikes of airy; the second collects words for open spaces and empty words.
note.cn: 第一组收与 airy 形近的词；第二组收「开阔」与「空洞」两义的近义词。

entries.definition: informal British word for impractical and vague ideas
entries.definitionCN: （英式口语）空想的；不切实际的

entries.definition: a literary variant of airy, also meaning an eagle's nest
entries.definitionCN: airy 的文学变体，亦指鹰巢

entries.definition: strange and frightening; only pronounced similarly, different root
entries.definitionCN: 诡异吓人的；仅与 airy 音近，词源不同

entries.definition: in a light, casual, or unconcerned way
entries.definitionCN: 轻快地；漫不经心地

entries.definition: large and with plenty of room inside
entries.definitionCN: 宽敞的；空间大的

entries.definition: with a light wind, or cheerful and relaxed
entries.definitionCN: 有微风的；轻松愉快的

entries.definition: not clear or precise, like airy promises
entries.definitionCN: 含糊的；不明确的

entries.definition: extremely light and delicate, seeming not of this world
entries.definitionCN: 轻盈飘渺的；超凡的

entries.definition: empty inside, as of hollow words
entries.definitionCN: 空心的；（话语）空洞的

normalIntro.en: The word is air plus -y: full of air, and so light.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 air 加 -y：满是空气，所以轻盈。

normal.en: An airy room lets the wind walk through it.
normal.cn: 通风的房间能让风穿堂而过。

normal.en: An airy wave is a light, careless little movement.
normal.cn: airy wave 是轻描淡写的小动作。

normal.en: Airy promises are made of air: nothing to hold.
normal.cn: 空洞的承诺是空气做的：抓不住任何东西。

normal.en: airy-fairy is the informal cousin for unrealistic ideas.
normal.cn: airy-fairy 是它的口语近亲，形容不切实际。

normal.en: airily is the adverb: she replied airily.
normal.cn: airily 是副词：她轻快地答道。

abstract.en: Picture curtains lifting in a tall white room.
abstract.cn: 想象高大的白房间里窗帘被风掀起。

abstract.en: See a girl waving as she drifts past, feet barely touching the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个女孩飘然而过，脚尖几乎不沾地。

abstract.en: Imagine grabbing at a soap bubble and finding your hand full of nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象去抓肥皂泡，摊开手却什么都没有。

examples.en: They chose the apartment for its airy rooms.
examples.cn: 他们选中这套公寓是因为房间明亮通风。

examples.en: He waved an airy hand and changed the subject.
examples.cn: 他随意地摆了摆手，转换了话题。

examples.en: The plan was dismissed as airy nonsense.
examples.cn: 这个计划被斥为空洞的空想。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿瑞」——爱儿住的房子通风又亮堂，心里舒坦得很。

root: 名词 air 源自希腊语 aer「低层大气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；16 世纪加形容词后缀 -y 构成 airy，由「通风」引申出「轻快」与「空洞」二义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses follow air itself: rooms full of it, manners as light as it, and ideas with nothing in them.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都跟着 air 走：满是空气的房间，像空气一样轻的举止，以及空无一物的想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open window in a white room, wind and light passing through, nothing held back.
core.cn: 核心意象：白屋敞窗，风与光穿堂而过，无一物滞留。

branches.en: tall windows pulling a breeze through a studio
branches.cn: 高窗把微风引进画室

branches.en: a light wave of the hand, feet barely on the ground
branches.cn: 轻描淡写的挥手，脚尖几乎不着地

branches.en: a speech full of promises and empty of plans
branches.cn: 满是承诺、空无方案的演讲

branches.en: the weightless manner and the weightless idea behind it
branches.cn: 没有分量的举止，与举止背后没有分量的想法

branches.en: one quality of air, filling rooms, gestures, and words
branches.cn: 空气的同一性质，充盈着房间、姿态与言辞

intro.en: A Greek-Latin noun for air plus the common English adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: 希腊-拉丁语源的名词 air，加常见英语形容词后缀 -y。

latinIntro.en: aer is the recorded Latin borrowing from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: aer 是有记录的拉丁语对希腊语的借用。

items.meaning: of the air, existing in the air

definition_zh: 同族的；类似的；与……性质相近
definition_en: related by blood, or very similar in character or quality
core_image: 同一棵树上的两根枝条：分开生长，血却是同一脉
scene: 他说这份孤独感他再熟悉不过了。Her silence that evening was akin to grief.
sceneCN: 这里 akin 是「与……性质相近」（第 2 个义项：性格或品质上极为相似）；句意是说她那晚的沉默近乎悲伤。

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「亲属；家族」；akin 由 a- 加 kin 构成
kin 加 -ship，义为「亲属关系；亲密感」
与 kin 同源的近亲词，义为「同类的；相关的」

senses.title: Related by blood
senses.definition: belonging to the same family by blood relationship
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘而属于同一家族
senses.example: She is akin to the old duke by marriage and by blood.
senses.exampleCN: 她与老公爵既有姻亲又有血缘关系。
senses.why: Akin is literally 'of one kin': the prefix a- is an old use of 'on' or 'in', so the word means 'in the same family'.
senses.whyCN: akin 字面即「同属一族」：前缀 a- 是古英语「在……之中」的用法，故本义为「在同一亲族之内」。

senses.title: Similar in character or quality
senses.definition: having similar qualities, as if belonging to the same family; usually with to
senses.definitionCN: 性质相似，仿佛同出一族；通常与 to 连用
senses.example: His excitement was akin to a child's on the morning of a holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 他的兴奋近乎孩子度假日清晨的那种心情。
senses.why: Two things with the same character are pictured as branches of one tree, so the family word stretches to likenesses of every kind.
senses.whyCN: 性质相同之物被想象成一棵树上的枝条，于是「家族」一词就延伸到一切相似性上。

intro.en: An old English phrase 'of one kin' frozen into a single adjective.
intro.cn: 古英语短语「of one kin（同族）」凝固成的一个形容词。

items.en: The reconstructed root *kunjam meant family, race, or people, the source of kin and kind.
items.cn: 重构词根 *kunjam 意为家族、种族、民族，是 kin 与 kind 的来源。

items.en: cyn meant kin, family, or nation, and cynnad meant related by blood.
items.cn: 古英语 cyn 指亲族、家族、民族，cynnad 意为「有血缘关系的」。

items.en: kin survived as the everyday word for relatives.
items.cn: 中古英语中 kin 仍是「亲属」的日常用词。

items.en: akin arose from the phrase of kin, with a- as a reduced form of on or of.
items.cn: 16 世纪 akin 由短语 of kin 缩合而来，a- 是 on 或 of 的弱化形式。

items.en: The blood sense survives in formal use; the 'similar to' sense, with to, is now the common one.
items.cn: 现代英语中血缘义保留于正式文体；与 to 连用的「相似」义已成为常用义。

note.en: The first group gathers the kin family and a spelling twin; the second gathers words for resemblance.
note.cn: 第一组收 kin 词族与一个拼写相近词；第二组收表示「相似」的词。

entries.definition: one's relatives and family
entries.definitionCN: 亲属；家族

entries.definition: blood relationship, or a feeling of close connection
entries.definitionCN: 亲属关系；亲密感

entries.definition: related or similar, as in kindred spirits
entries.definitionCN: 同族的；志趣相投的（如 kindred spirits）

entries.definition: a medical term for lack of movement; only looks similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: （医学）运动不能的；仅拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: alike in appearance or nature though not identical
entries.definitionCN: 相似的；相仿的

entries.definition: able to be compared because of shared qualities
entries.definitionCN: 可比较的；类似的

entries.definition: similar in function or position though different in origin
entries.definitionCN: 功能或地位相似的；类似的

entries.definition: connected by family or by shared origin
entries.definitionCN: 有亲属关系的；相关的

entries.definition: of the same nature, as in kindred minds
entries.definitionCN: 同类的；心意相通的

normalIntro.en: The word is a- plus kin: of the same family, in blood or in nature.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 a- 加 kin：血缘上或性质上同属一家。

normal.en: kin means family, so akin is literally 'one family'.
normal.cn: kin 是家族，akin 字面就是「一家人」。

normal.en: akin to is the fixed pattern: silence akin to grief.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 akin to：近乎悲伤的沉默。

normal.en: kindred spirits are people akin to you in mind.
normal.cn: kindred spirits 就是在心性上与你 akin 的人。

normal.en: The blood sense appears in formal writing about dynasties.
normal.cn: 血缘义多见于正式文字，如王朝谱系。

normal.en: kinship is the noun behind the feeling of being akin.
normal.cn: kinship 是「同属一家」这种感受的名词形式。

abstract.en: Picture two branches high on one trunk, neither touching the other.
abstract.cn: 想象同一根树干上两根高处的枝条，彼此并不相触。

abstract.en: See two strangers discovering they were born in the same street.
abstract.cn: 想象两个陌生人发现彼此生在同一条街。

abstract.en: Imagine a feeling that is almost, but not quite, fear.
abstract.cn: 想象一种近乎恐惧、却又不全是恐惧的感觉。

examples.en: Pride that curdles into cruelty is akin to madness.
examples.cn: 发酵成残忍的傲慢近乎疯狂。

examples.en: The two languages are closely akin.
examples.cn: 这两种语言极为相近。

examples.en: He felt something akin to pity for the defeated general.
examples.cn: 他对那位败将感到近乎怜悯的情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额kin」——额头撞额头才知道，我们本是自家人，性子也像。

root: akin 由短语 of kin 缩合而成：kin 源自古英语 cyn「家族、种族」，可追溯至原始日耳曼语 *kunjam；前缀 a- 为 on 或 of 的弱化形式，本义「同族」，后引申为「性质相近」。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses keep one family picture: literal blood relations, then anything so like another it might share the same line.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用一幅「家族」图景：先是真实的血缘，再是一切像到仿佛同宗的相似。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two branches of one tree, growing apart yet sharing a single root.
core.cn: 核心意象：一树两枝，各自生长，却同出一根。

branches.en: cousins traced through an old family register
branches.cn: 家谱上追认的表亲

branches.en: a silence that feels almost like grief
branches.cn: 近乎悲伤的沉默

branches.en: two dialects so alike they share old songs
branches.cn: 像到共享古歌谣的两种方言

branches.en: the same root claimed by blood or by likeness
branches.cn: 同一条根：或凭血缘，或凭相似

branches.en: kindred spirits meeting for the first time
branches.cn: 初次见面却如故人的知音

intro.en: A Germanic family noun inside an old prefix, plus the same family's later English offspring.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语家族名词套上古老前缀，外加同一家族在英语中的后代词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root here; the family is Germanic from *kunjam onwards.
latinIntro.cn: 此处没有拉丁词根；自 *kunjam 以下全是日耳曼血统。

items.meaning: of the same nature or origin
sort, type; or showing a good nature

definition_zh: 敏捷；乐意；欣然
definition_en: brisk and cheerful readiness to do something
core_image: 一声令下立刻起跑的猎犬：腿快，心也快
scene: 教练刚喊完集合，他已经穿好钉鞋站在跑道上了。She accepted the extra assignment with alacrity.
sceneCN: 这里 alacrity 是「乐意、欣然」（第 2 个义项：愉快而敏捷的响应）；句意是她欣然接受了额外的任务。

derivatives.zh: alacrity 的形容词形式（罕用），义为「敏捷的；乐意的」
同源结构的姊妹词，来自拉丁 celeritas 加 -ity，义为「迅速；敏捷」（词源相关，非同根）

senses.title: Briskness of movement or response
senses.definition: quick, lively speed in acting or answering
senses.definitionCN: 行动或应答的迅捷与活泼
senses.example: The dog sprang up with alacrity at the whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 哨声一响，狗立刻敏捷地跳起来。
senses.why: The Latin base alacer meant lively and quick, so the noun first names physical briskness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 alacer 意为「活泼敏捷」，名词最初便指动作上的麻利。

senses.title: Cheerful readiness of mind
senses.definition: eagerness and willingness, a cheerful promptness to agree or comply
senses.definitionCN: 热切的自愿，愉快爽快地答应或顺从
senses.example: He accepted the invitation with alacrity.
senses.exampleCN: 他欣然接受了邀请。
senses.why: A lively spirit is also a willing one, so the quickness of the body widened into eagerness of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 活泼的精神也是愿意的精神，身体的敏捷便扩展为心灵的踊跃。

intro.en: From a Latin adjective meaning lively, kept almost unchanged in form by English.
intro.cn: 来自一个意为「活泼」的拉丁形容词，英语几乎原样保留了它的形态。

items.en: A reconstructed root *h₂el- expressed movement, energy, or nourishment; the exact line is uncertain.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h₂el- 或与运动、能量、滋养相关，具体路径不确定。

items.en: alacer meant lively, brisk, and eager, applied to both bodies and minds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alacer 意为「活泼、敏捷、热切」，可形容身体与心神。

items.en: alacritas named liveliness and eagerness as a quality.
items.cn: alacritas 指「活泼、踊跃」这一品质。

items.en: English took alacritas directly as alacrity, first with the Latin sense of liveliness.
items.cn: 15 世纪英语直接借入 alacritas 作 alacrity，最初保留「活泼」义。

items.en: Today the word almost always means cheerful willingness, usually after with.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词几乎总指「欣然乐意」，常与 with 连用。

note.en: The first group holds a rare sibling word and an unrelated look-alike; the second holds words for eagerness.
note.cn: 第一组收一个罕用同族词与一个无关的形近词；第二组收表示「热切」的词。

entries.definition: a rare adjective form meaning lively and willing
entries.definitionCN: 罕用形容词，意为「活泼乐意的」

entries.definition: a set phrase using the noun itself
entries.definitionCN: 使用该名词的固定说法「精神的踊跃」

entries.definition: bold daring; only looks and sounds similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 大胆放肆；仅形音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: keen desire to do or have something
entries.definitionCN: 渴望；热切

entries.definition: willingness to act at once
entries.definitionCN: 愿意；随时准备行动

entries.definition: the quality of acting quickly and without delay
entries.definitionCN: 迅速；果断

entries.definition: the state of being glad to comply
entries.definitionCN: 自愿；乐意

entries.definition: intense enjoyment and interest, stronger and warmer than brisk readiness
entries.definitionCN: 热情；兴致，比爽快应允更炽热

normalIntro.en: From Latin alacer, lively: a mind that jumps up like a quick dog.
normalIntro.cn: 来自拉丁语 alacer「活泼」：一颗像灵犬一样立刻起跳的心。

normal.en: with alacrity is the classic exam phrase.
normal.cn: with alacrity 是考试经典搭配。

normal.en: alacer meant lively; alacrity keeps the bounce.
normal.cn: alacer 意为活泼，alacrity 保留了那份弹跳感。

normal.en: It combines speed and gladness in one word.
normal.cn: 它把「快」与「乐」合在一个词里。

normal.en: People accept invitations with alacrity, not reluctance.
normal.cn: 人们欣然受邀，而不是勉为其难。

normal.en: Compare audacity, daring, a different word that merely looks alike.
normal.cn: 对比 audacity「大胆」，只是形近而已。

abstract.en: Picture a dog already running before the whistle ends.
abstract.cn: 想象哨声未落，狗已经跑出去了。

abstract.en: See a hand shooting up before the teacher finishes the question.
abstract.cn: 想象老师问题还没问完，一只手已经举起。

abstract.en: Imagine the sound of eager feet on stairs going up two at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象上楼时一步两级的热切脚步声。

examples.en: She agreed to help with unfeigned alacrity.
examples.cn: 她毫不做作地欣然答应帮忙。

examples.en: The troops moved with alacrity when the order came.
examples.cn: 命令一到，部队闻令即动。

examples.en: He volunteered with alacrity for the hardest task.
examples.cn: 他踊跃请缨承担最艰巨的任务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿拉渴力」——阿拉（我们）渴了也有力气，一喊就来，干劲十足。

root: 拉丁语 alacer「活泼敏捷的」派生名词 alacritas「踊跃」，15 世纪直接借入英语作 alacrity；更早词基可溯至重构形式 *h₂el-，存疑。本义为身体敏捷，现代常用义转为心甘情愿的爽快。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses split one lively energy: quickness of the limbs, then gladness of the will.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项把同一种活泼的能量一分为二：一是手脚的麻利，二是心意的甘愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog already running before the whistle finishes.
core.cn: 核心意象：哨声未落，狗已飞奔而出。

branches.en: a whistled command answered in mid-air
branches.cn: 哨令未完已腾空而起的应答

branches.en: sailors running up the rigging at once
branches.cn: 水手们即刻攀上索具

branches.en: an acceptance letter sent back the same afternoon
branches.cn: 当天下午就寄回的应允信

branches.en: volunteering for the hardest job before it is described
branches.cn: 任务还没讲完就踊跃请缨

branches.en: one eager energy, in the legs and in the heart
branches.cn: 同一股热望，在腿上，也在心里

intro.en: A Latin adjective of liveliness with its noun ending, borrowed whole.
intro.cn: 一个表示「活泼」的拉丁形容词连其名词词尾被整体借入。

latinIntro.en: alacer and alacritas are recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: alacer 与 alacritas 都是有记录的拉丁形态。

definition_zh: 虽然；尽管
definition_en: although, used to introduce a phrase that admits something while qualifying the main statement
core_image: 一句话说完，又回头补上一句「虽然如此」，把话说得更稳
scene: 方案被改得只剩三页，讨论却还没开始。The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
sceneCN: 这里 albeit 是「虽然、尽管」（第 1 个义项：引导让步短语，表示前面的话要打个折扣）；句意为方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。图中可辨识物件：三页方案、长桌、批注笔。

derivatives.zh: albeit 的原始三词形式，义为「尽管它是……」
同一构词模式的古旧连词，义为「虽然；然而」

senses.title: Although, before a phrase
senses.definition: although, used chiefly before an adjective, adverb, or prepositional phrase to concede a point
senses.definitionCN: 意为「虽然」，多用于形容词、副词或介词短语之前，表示让步
senses.example: The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。
senses.why: Albeit is a compressed clause, 'all be it', so it can carry only a small phrase: what follows is the thing that 'is' conceded.
senses.whyCN: albeit 是一个压缩的从句「all be it」，所以只能带一个小短语：后面跟的就是被承认「是」的那一点。

senses.title: Although, before a full clause, in older use
senses.titleCN: 虽然（后接完整从句的古旧用法）
senses.definition: in older writing, although, used before a full clause with its own subject and verb
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的文字中意为「虽然」，后面可以接带主语和动词的完整从句
senses.example: Albeit he was tired, he stayed until the end.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管他很累，还是留到了最后。
senses.why: Because the word still contains 'it', older writers could let a whole clause follow; modern usage prefers although for that job.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词里仍含有 it，旧时作者可以接一整个从句；现代用法则把这个任务交给 although。

intro.en: Albeit is a whole clause worn down into one word: 'all be it' became a single concessive conjunction.
intro.cn: albeit 是一整个从句磨损成一个词：「all be it」变成了单一的让步连词。

items.en: The phrase all be it meant 'though it be all (that)', a concessive clause used after a statement.
items.cn: 短语 all be it 意为「尽管它是这样」，是放在陈述之后的让步从句。

items.en: Reduced forms such as al be it appear in the fourteenth century, with al as a variant of all.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现 al be it 这类缩减形式，其中 al 是 all 的变体。

items.en: The three words fuse into albeit, and the new word is felt as a single conjunction.
items.cn: 三个词融合成 albeit，新词被当作一个整体连词来使用。

items.en: Albeit is common in formal prose, often introducing a short phrase rather than a clause.
items.cn: albeit 在正式散文中常见，多引导短短语而不是完整从句。

items.en: The word survives mainly in careful writing, where its brevity is valued over the plainer although.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在讲究的文字里，人们看重它比 although 更简洁。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same 'be it' pattern; the near-meaning group gathers concessive connectors.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「be it」模式构成的词；近义组收表示让步的连接词。

entries.definition: An archaic conjunction meaning although or nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧连词，意为「虽然」或「然而」。

entries.definition: An archaic conjunction meaning provided that.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧连词，意为「只要；倘若」。

entries.definition: The standard conjunction for conceding a fact before the main clause.
entries.definitionCN: 在主句前承认某一事实的标准连词。

entries.definition: A shorter and more informal form of although, also usable at the end of a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: although 更短更口语的形式，也可放在句末。

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, more neutral than a concession.
entries.definitionCN: 用于对比两项事实，比让步更中性。

normalIntro.en: Three real words carry it: all, be, and it, worn down into one conjunction.
normalIntro.cn: 三个真实词承载它：all、be、it，磨损成一个连词。

normal.en: Albeit is all be it: say the three words fast and the conjunction appears.
normal.cn: albeit 就是 all be it：把三个词连快说，连词就出来了。

normal.en: Because it contains be, it likes short phrases rather than full clauses.
normal.cn: 因为里面含有 be，它更爱接短短语而不是完整从句。

normal.en: Albeit is one word, never two: no comma inside it.
normal.cn: albeit 是一个词，不是两个：中间不加逗号。

normal.en: Use albeit for a concession you want to keep brief; use although when a clause follows.
normal.cn: 想简短地让一步就用 albeit；后面跟完整从句时用 although。

normal.en: The stress falls at the end: al-BE-it.
normal.cn: 重音落在末尾：al-BE-it。

abstract.en: A three-word clause collapsed into one word shows how grammar compresses repeated thought.
abstract.cn: 三个词的从句缩成一个词，说明语法会压缩反复出现的想法。

abstract.en: Albeit admits a limitation without withdrawing the claim, which is a very precise social move.
abstract.cn: albeit 承认一个限制，却不撤回主张，这是一种非常精确的社交动作。

abstract.en: The word now sounds formal because plain although does the same work more cheaply.
abstract.cn: 这个词如今显得正式，因为朴素的 although 用更低的成本完成了同样的事。

examples.en: The plan was accepted, albeit with several conditions.
examples.cn: 方案被接受了，尽管附有几个条件。

examples.en: He agreed to help, albeit reluctantly.
examples.cn: 他同意帮忙，尽管很不情愿。

examples.en: The team won the match, albeit by a single point.
examples.cn: 球队赢了比赛，尽管只赢了一分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，必特」——噢，必特先生答应了，虽然有点勉强。

root: 源自中古英语短语 all be it「尽管它是」，三个词融合为一个让步连词。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses concede a point; the only difference is how much grammar the word is allowed to carry after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在让一步，区别只在于这个词后面能带多少语法成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence finishes, then a hand goes back to add 'even so' at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话说完，一只手又回去在边上补一句「即便如此」。

branches.en: a yes followed by a list of conditions
branches.cn: 一个「同意」后面跟着一串条件

branches.en: a slow yes, said with a sigh
branches.cn: 叹着气说出的那个「好」

branches.en: an old sentence with a full clause after it
branches.cn: 后面接着完整从句的旧式句子

branches.en: a page of seventeenth-century prose
branches.cn: 十七世纪散文的一页

branches.en: one concession, now short and now long
branches.cn: 同一个让步，有时短，有时长

intro.en: Three ordinary English words fused into a single conjunction.
intro.cn: 三个普通英语单词融合成一个连词。

latinIntro.en: Every part is native English; there is no Latin layer, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 每个成分都是英语本族词，没有拉丁语层，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

definition_zh: 音乐专辑；相册；集邮册；签名纪念册；（古罗马）白色公告板
definition_en: a collection of recorded songs issued together, a book for keeping photographs, stamps or signatures, or the whitened board on which public notices were written in ancient Rome
core_image: 一本硬壳大书摊在膝上，纸页里贴着一排排小方片
scene: 客厅的矮柜里躺着一本硬壳大书，翻开是婚礼那天的照片，边角已经微微发黄。She opened the album and found a photograph of her grandmother at twenty.
sceneCN: 这里 album 是「相册」（第 2 个义项：收集照片的册子）；句意为她翻开相册，找到一张祖母二十岁时的照片。画面里是矮柜、硬壳书与泛黄的照片。

pos.zh: 名词：音乐专辑；相册；集邮册；签名纪念册；古罗马公告板

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 mini- 与 album 组合而成，义为「迷你专辑」，指曲目较少、时长较短的发行形式
由 album 与 -oriented 组合而成，义为「以专辑为导向的」，多用于描述电台的编排格式

senses.title: A collection of recorded songs
senses.titleCN: 音乐专辑：成套发行的录音作品
senses.definition: a set of recorded songs or pieces released together as one work, on disc, tape or in digital form
senses.definitionCN: 作为一件作品成套发行的录音歌曲或乐曲，载体可以是唱片、磁带或数字文件
senses.example: Their second album sold a million copies in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的第二张专辑一个月内卖出一百万张。
senses.why: Early records were sold in a book-like sleeve holding several discs, so the container's name moved onto the collection of songs inside it.
senses.whyCN: 早期的唱片装在一个像书一样、能装几张唱片的封套里，于是容器的名字转移到了里面那一组歌曲上。

senses.title: A book of photographs
senses.definition: a book with blank pages or pockets in which photographs are kept
senses.definitionCN: 有空白页或插袋、用来存放照片的册子
senses.example: The wedding album sat on the shelf for years without being opened.
senses.exampleCN: 那本婚礼相册在书架上放了好几年都没被翻开。
senses.why: Album first meant a blank surface for writing, and photographs are simply what people began pasting onto that blank surface.
senses.whyCN: album 最初指可供书写的空白表面，而照片不过是人们后来贴到这个空白表面上的东西。

senses.title: A book for stamps and clippings
senses.titleCN: 集邮册：贴存邮票与剪报的册子
senses.definition: a book with pages for mounting stamps, postcards, newspaper cuttings or other small flat items
senses.definitionCN: 页面可固定邮票、明信片、剪报或其他小件平面收藏品的册子
senses.example: He pasted every foreign stamp into a green album.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每一枚外国邮票都贴进一本绿色集邮册。
senses.why: The same blank book serves any small flat treasure, so stamps and clippings simply repeat the collecting gesture that photographs had already taught.
senses.whyCN: 同一本空白册子可以服务任何小件平面收藏品，于是邮票与剪报只是重复照片已经教会人们的那个「收集」动作。

senses.title: A book of signatures and memories
senses.titleCN: 签名纪念册：留字留念的册子
senses.definition: a book in which friends, guests or classmates write their names, wishes or short messages as a keepsake
senses.definitionCN: 请朋友、来客或同学写下姓名、祝愿或短句以作留念的册子
senses.example: Her classmates filled an album with wishes before she moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬走之前，同学们在一本纪念册里写满了祝福。
senses.why: This is the oldest modern use: a blank book passed from hand to hand, so that the writing itself becomes the collection.
senses.whyCN: 这是这本书最早的现代用法：一本空白册子在人们手中传递，写下的字本身就成了被收藏的内容。

senses.title: The whitened notice board of Rome
senses.titleCN: 古罗马白色公告板：张贴公告的涂白木板
senses.definition: in ancient Rome, a board whitened with gypsum on which public notices, lists and announcements were written
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马用石膏涂白的木板，上面书写公告、名单与通告
senses.example: In Rome a notice of the games was painted on an album in the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 在罗马，竞技公告被写在广场的一块白色公告板上。
senses.why: The Latin word named a whitened board before it named a book, and this is the literal image from which every later collection sense grows.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词先指涂白的木板，后指册子；正是这块板子的具体形象，长出了后来所有的「收集」义。

intro.en: Album comes straight from Latin, where it began as a whitened board and ended as a blank book.
intro.cn: album 直接来自拉丁语，在那里它先是一块涂白的木板，后来才成为空白册子。

items.en: Albus was the adjective for white or pale; it is the colour word behind the whole family, including albedo and albino.
items.cn: albus 是表示「白色、苍白」的形容词，是 albedo、albino 等一整族词背后的颜色词。

items.en: The neuter noun album meant a white tablet or board, especially one whitened with gypsum for public notices and lists.
items.cn: 中性名词 album 指白色的板或牌，尤指用石膏涂白、供书写公告与名单的木板。

items.en: Medieval Latin extended album from the board to the written list itself, and then to a blank book or register kept for entries.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把 album 从木板扩展到写在上面的名单，再扩展到供人题写的空白册子或登记簿。

items.en: English album is recorded in the seventeenth century for a blank book in which friends wrote names and verses; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 album 在十七世纪有记录，指供朋友写下姓名与赠言的空白册子；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Photograph and stamp albums belong to the nineteenth century; the recorded-music album grew out of book-like record sleeves in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 照片相册与集邮册属于十九世纪；唱片专辑则从二十世纪那种像书一样的唱片封套中发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin colour root albus; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of collected works and books.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁颜色词根 albus 的一族词；近义组收其他类型的作品合集与册子。

entries.definition: The proportion of light a surface reflects; a scientific word built on Latin albus, white.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反照率、反射率」，指表面反射光的比例；由拉丁语 albus「白」构成。

entries.definition: A person or animal born with no pigment in skin, hair or eyes; formed from the same white root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「白化病患者、白化动物」，指出生时皮肤、毛发或眼睛缺少色素者；同出「白」这一词根。

entries.definition: The white of an egg; the Latin noun albumen also meant egg white, from albus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛋白、蛋清」；拉丁语 albumen 本也指蛋清，源自 albus。

entries.definition: A white linen robe worn by priests; a church word from the Latin adjective for white.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「白麻布长袍」，是神职人员穿的礼服；来自拉丁语表示白色的形容词。

entries.definition: A collection of pieces gathered from various sources into one work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合集、汇编」，指从不同来源收集作品编成一册或一张。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for pasting in photographs, cuttings and small keepsakes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剪贴簿」，指空白页可粘贴照片、剪报与小纪念品的册子。

entries.definition: A published collection of poems or stories by different writers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选集、诗文集」，指把不同作者的诗或小说编在一起出版的书。

entries.definition: A flat case, or the set of works it holds, used to show an artist's or designer's output.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「作品集、画夹」，指装作品的扁平夹子或其中展示艺术家成果的一组作品。

entries.definition: A disc carrying recorded sound; the physical object an album is played from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「唱片」，指承载录音的圆盘，即播放专辑所用的实物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root albus, the board-to-book history, and the phrases album appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 albus、从木板到册子的词义史，以及 album 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Albus means white: the first album was a board whitened with gypsum so that notices would stand out.
normal.cn: albus 意为白色：最早的 album 是一块用石膏涂白的木板，好让公告更醒目。

normal.en: The word moved from board to list to blank book, which is why a photo album and a stamp album feel like the same object.
normal.cn: 这个词从木板走到名单，再走到空白册子，所以相册与集邮册感觉是同一种东西。

normal.en: Albedo, albino and albumen all keep the white idea, though their meanings moved far from paper.
normal.cn: albedo、albino、albumen 都保留了「白」的观念，尽管词义已经远离纸张。

normal.en: A studio album is recorded in a studio; a debut album is the first one a band releases.
normal.cn: studio album 是在录音室录的专辑；debut album 是乐队发行的第一张。

normal.en: The album cover is the book cover of this modern book of songs.
normal.cn: album cover 就是这本现代「歌本」的封面。

abstract.en: Picture a white board in a Roman square, then the same white surface bound into pages.
abstract.cn: 想象罗马广场上的一块白板，再想象同一片白色被装订成页。

abstract.en: The pages can hold photographs, stamps, signatures or songs; the container stays, the contents change.
abstract.cn: 这些页面可以装照片、邮票、签名或歌曲；容器不变，内容不断更换。

abstract.en: An album is an argument that separate small things belong together.
abstract.cn: album 本身就是一个主张：一件件小东西应当被放在一起。

examples.en: Their second album sold a million copies.
examples.cn: 他们的第二张专辑卖出了一百万张。

examples.en: She keeps every holiday photo in a thick album.
examples.cn: 她把每张假日照片都收在一本厚相册里。

examples.en: The band is recording a new album in London.
examples.cn: 乐队正在伦敦录制一张新专辑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿尔本」——阿尔白白的，本子也白白的：先贴公告，再贴照片与歌。

root: album 直接借自拉丁语 album，本义是「涂白的板」，来自形容词 albus「白色」。古罗马人把公告写在涂了石膏的白板上，中世纪拉丁语再由「白板上的名单」引申为空白登记册，英语十七世纪用它指题字留念的册子，十九世纪起指相册与集邮册，二十世纪又指唱片专辑。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses are the same blank surface: a whitened board for notices, then a blank book for signatures, photographs, stamps, and finally a sleeve for songs.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都是同一片空白表面：先是贴公告的白板，再是题字、贴照片、贴邮票的空白册子，最后是装歌曲的封套。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white board waits for writing, and later the same white surface is bound into pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块白板等着被书写，后来同一片白色被装订成了书页。

branches.en: THE SONGS: a book-like sleeve holds discs, and its name passes to the songs inside.
branches.cn: 歌曲线：像书一样的封套装着唱片，名字便转到了里面的歌曲上。

branches.en: THE PHOTOGRAPHS: the blank page becomes a place to keep images.
branches.cn: 照片线：空白页面成了保存影像的地方。

branches.en: THE STAMPS: any small flat treasure can be pasted onto the same page.
branches.cn: 邮票线：任何小件平面收藏品都能贴到同样的页面上。

branches.en: THE SIGNATURES: friends write on the blank page, and the writing itself is the collection.
branches.cn: 签名线：朋友在空白页上写字，写下的字本身就是收藏。

branches.en: THE BOARD: the Roman notice board is the literal white surface behind every later sense.
branches.cn: 木板线：古罗马的公告板是后来所有义项背后那片具体的白色表面。

intro.en: Album is a Latin noun with a Latin adjective inside it; English adds combining forms and suffixes to build new words around it.
intro.cn: album 是一个内含拉丁形容词的拉丁名词；英语再用组合形式与后缀在它周围造新词。

latinIntro.en: Albus, album, albumen and albedo are all recorded Latin forms, so nothing in this family needs to be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: albus、album、albumen 与 albedo 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，这一族词无需重构。

items.example: Albus is the colour word inside album.
items.exampleCN: albus 是 album 里面的那个颜色词。

items.example: The root appears in albino and albedo.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在 albino 与 albedo 里。

items.example: The Latin noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the gender of Latin album.
items.exampleCN: 它标出拉丁语 album 的性。

items.meaningCN: 构成 albumen 这类名词的词尾

latinEntries.meaning: a white board for notices; a register

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 mini- 与 album 组合而成，义为「迷你专辑」
由 album 与 -oriented 组合而成，义为「以专辑为导向的」

definition_zh: 炼金术；点石成金的技艺；神奇的转化力
definition_en: a medieval practice of trying to change base metals into gold, or any seemingly magical power of transformation
core_image: 幽暗地窖里的坩埚：铅在火中等待变成黄金的那一刻
scene: 地窖深处，炉火映着满墙的符文手稿。Medieval alchemy sought to turn lead into gold.
sceneCN: 这里 alchemy 是「炼金术」（第 1 个义项：中世纪试图把贱金属变成黄金的方术）；句意是中世纪炼金术试图将铅变成黄金。

collocations.zh: 金融炼金术（虚幻的生财之道）

derivatives.zh: alchemy 加表示人的后缀 -ist，义为「炼金术士」
alchemy 加形容词后缀 -ical，义为「炼金术的；神奇的」
与 alchemy 同源的姊妹词，经阿拉伯语辗转传入，义为「化学」

senses.title: The medieval art of transmutation
senses.definition: the old practice of trying to turn common metals into gold and to find a universal cure
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪试图将贱金属炼成黄金并寻求万灵药的方术
senses.example: Princes kept alchemists hoping that alchemy would refill their treasuries.
senses.exampleCN: 君主们供养炼金术士，指望炼金术能填满国库。
senses.why: The Arabic article al- plus kīmiyā names the craft directly: 'the art of transmutation'.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语定冠词 al- 加 kīmiyā 直接点明这门技艺：「转化之术」。

senses.title: Any seemingly magical transformation
senses.definition: a process that changes something in a mysterious or wonderful way
senses.definitionCN: 以神秘或奇妙的方式改变事物的过程
senses.example: There is a kind of alchemy in the way this kitchen turns leftovers into feasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这间厨房能把剩菜变成盛宴，简直有点石成金之妙。
senses.why: If alchemists could raise lead to gold, any astonishing upgrade earns the same name by metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 既然炼金术士能把铅炼成金，任何惊人的升华便可借喻得名。

intro.en: A Greek word for 'poured matter' that travelled through Arabic with its article fused on, then grew into both alchemy and chemistry.
intro.cn: 一个希腊词「浇注之物」，经阿拉伯语时冠词与之熔为一体传入欧洲，后来分出 alchemy 与 chemistry 两个词。

items.en: khēmeia or khumeia meant the art of pouring and mixing, later of transmuting metals; the exact spelling is debated.
items.cn: 希腊语 khēmeia 或 khumeia 意为「浇注混合之术」，后指金属转化术；拼写尚有争议。

items.en: Arabic al-kīmiyāʾ fused the definite article al- onto the borrowed word.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kīmiyāʾ 把定冠词 al- 熔接在借词之上。

items.en: Latin alchemia carried the Arabic form into European scholarship.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 把阿拉伯语形式带入欧洲学术。

items.en: Old French alquemie passed the word to English in the 14th century.
items.cn: 古法语 alquemie 于 14 世纪将该词传给英语。

items.en: The sibling chemistry split off for the science, leaving alchemy to the old art and its metaphor.
items.cn: 其姊妹词 chemistry 分出指称科学，alchemy 留给古方术及其比喻义。

note.en: The first group gathers the word's own offspring and sound-alikes; the second gathers words for mysterious transformation.
note.cn: 第一组收该词的后代词与音近词；第二组收表示「神秘转化」的词。

entries.definition: a person who practises alchemy
entries.definitionCN: 炼金术士

entries.definition: the science of substances, grown out of the same Arabic-Greek word
entries.definitionCN: 化学；与 alchemy 同出一源的姊妹词

entries.definition: an illusion or impossible fantasy; only sounds somewhat similar, unrelated root
entries.definitionCN: 幻想；空想；仅音近，词源无关

entries.definition: relating to alchemy, or magically transformative
entries.definitionCN: 炼金术的；有神奇转化力的

entries.definition: supernatural power, or an enchanting quality
entries.definitionCN: 魔法；魅力

entries.definition: the act of changing one thing into another, the literal goal of alchemy
entries.definitionCN: 嬗变；转化，炼金术的字面目标

entries.definition: the use of magic, often with dark overtones
entries.definitionCN: 巫术；妖术，常带阴暗色彩

entries.definition: magical skill, or extraordinary technical skill
entries.definitionCN: 魔法技艺；（喻）高超本领

entries.definition: a thorough or dramatic change in form or nature
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的改变；变形

normalIntro.en: The al- is the Arabic article 'the', and the rest became chemistry too.
normalIntro.cn: al- 是阿拉伯语定冠词「the」，剩下的部分后来又派生了 chemistry。

normal.en: alchemy and chemistry are twins from one Arabic word.
normal.cn: alchemy 与 chemistry 是同一个阿拉伯词的双生子。

normal.en: alchemist is the person, alchemical the adjective.
normal.cn: alchemist 是人，alchemical 是形容词。

normal.en: Many al- words came from Arabic: alcohol, algebra, alkali.
normal.cn: 许多 al- 开头的词都来自阿拉伯语：alcohol、algebra、alkali。

normal.en: The goal was transmutation: lead into gold.
normal.cn: 其目标是嬗变：点铅成金。

normal.en: Figuratively, alchemy is any wonderful upgrading.
normal.cn: 比喻义上，alchemy 指任何奇妙的升华。

abstract.en: Picture a bubbling crucible glowing orange in a dark cellar.
abstract.cn: 想象幽暗地窖里咕嘟作响、泛着橙光的坩埚。

abstract.en: See grey lead sinking into the pot and a gold coin rising out.
abstract.cn: 想象灰铅沉入锅底，一枚金币浮出水面。

abstract.en: Imagine yesterday's scraps arriving at the table as a banquet.
abstract.cn: 想象昨天的剩料上桌时已成一场盛宴。

examples.en: Isaac Newton devoted years to alchemy.
examples.cn: 牛顿曾花费多年研究炼金术。

examples.en: The novel describes the alchemy of grief into art.
examples.cn: 这部小说描写了把悲恸炼成艺术的转化。

examples.en: Critics dismissed the budget as financial alchemy.
examples.cn: 批评者斥这份预算为金融炼金术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱啊渴没」——爱金如渴的术士，最后炼金术没成，化学成了。

root: 希腊语 khēmeia/khumeia「浇注混合之术」借入阿拉伯语为 al-kīmiyāʾ（冠词 al- 熔合），经中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 与古法语 alquemie 于 14 世纪进入英语；同源姊妹词 chemistry 后指科学。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses run from furnace to metaphor: the literal art of making gold, then any wonderful change worth the same name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项从熔炉走向比喻：先是炼金本业，再是一切当得起此名的奇妙转变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crucible in a dark cellar, lead waiting to become gold.
core.cn: 核心意象：幽暗地窖中的坩埚，铅在等待成为黄金。

branches.en: a royal alchemist at a smoking furnace
branches.cn: 在冒着烟的炉前劳作的御用炼金术士

branches.en: manuscripts of symbols and formulas for gold
branches.cn: 写满炼金符号与配方的手稿

branches.en: a kitchen turning scraps into a feast
branches.cn: 把剩料变成盛宴的厨房

branches.en: grief refined into music
branches.cn: 被提炼成音乐的悲恸

branches.en: one promised transformation, in metal or in life
branches.cn: 同一种被许诺的转化，或在金属，或在人生

intro.en: An Arabic definite article welded to a Greek root, with English endings building the family.
intro.cn: 阿拉伯语定冠词焊接在希腊词根上，英语词尾再构筑词族。

latinIntro.en: alchemia is the medieval Latin form through which the word arrived.
latinIntro.cn: alchemia 是该词传入时经由的中世纪拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 酒精；乙醇；含酒精饮料；（化学）醇
definition_en: the colourless liquid in drinks that makes people drunk, drinks containing it, or a class of chemical compounds
core_image: 一只玻璃瓶里透明的液体，标签上只有一行成分说明
scene: 餐桌上摆着一排玻璃杯，有人正往里倒透明液体，冰块碰出轻响。The doctor asked how much alcohol he drank each week.
sceneCN: 这里 alcohol 是「酒精、含酒精饮料」（第 2 个义项：含有乙醇的饮品）；句意为医生问他每周喝多少酒。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、冰块、酒瓶。

pos.zh: 名词：酒精；乙醇；含酒精饮料；（化学）醇

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「含酒精的；酗酒的」
由本词加表示病态的 suffix 构成，义为「酒精中毒；酗酒成瘾」
由本词与 free 合成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: The intoxicating substance itself
senses.definition: the colourless liquid, ethanol, that is the active substance in drinks and is also used as a solvent
senses.definitionCN: 无色液体乙醇，是酒类中的有效成分，也用作溶剂
senses.example: This cleaner contains alcohol and should not be used near a flame.
senses.exampleCN: 这种清洁剂含酒精，不应在明火附近使用。
senses.why: This is the chemical sense, and it comes straight from the Arabic word for a fine powder once used as eye make-up: the liquid was first obtained by distillation.
senses.whyCN: 这是化学义，直接来自阿拉伯语中一种曾作眼影的细粉之名：这种液体最早正是通过蒸馏取得的。

senses.title: Drinks that contain it
senses.definition: drinks such as beer, wine, or spirits that contain ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 啤酒、葡萄酒、烈酒等含乙醇的饮品
senses.example: The doctor asked how much alcohol he drank each week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问他每周喝多少酒。
senses.why: Since the substance is what makes a drink alcoholic, the name of the substance became a general word for the drinks themselves.
senses.whyCN: 既然正是这种物质让饮品带酒劲，物质之名便成了一类饮品的总称。

senses.title: A class of chemical compounds
senses.definition: in chemistry, any of a large class of organic compounds containing a hydroxyl group
senses.definitionCN: 化学中含有羟基的一类有机化合物
senses.example: Sugar alcohols are used as sweeteners in many processed foods.
senses.exampleCN: 糖醇被用作许多加工食品的甜味剂。
senses.why: Chemists generalised the name from ethanol to the whole family, so any compound built on the same pattern counts as an alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 化学家把这个名字从乙醇推广到整个家族，凡是按同一结构组成的化合物都算一种 alcohol。

intro.en: Alcohol began as an Arabic word for a fine powder used as eye make-up, and only later became the name of a distilled liquid.
intro.cn: alcohol 原是一个阿拉伯语词，指用作眼影的细粉，后来才成为蒸馏液体的名称。

items.en: Al-kuhl named a fine powder of antimony used to darken the eyelids, and by extension anything finely refined.
items.cn: al-kuḥl 指一种用于描黑眼睑的锑粉，并引申指任何精细提炼之物。

items.en: Alchemists borrowed the word for a finely purified substance, and used it for spirits obtained by distillation.
items.cn: 炼金术士借这个词指精细提纯之物，并用它称呼蒸馏所得的烈性液体。

items.en: English alcohol first names a powder and then, from the sixteenth century, a distilled spirit.
items.cn: 英语 alcohol 先指粉末，十六世纪起指蒸馏酒。

items.en: Chemistry fixed the word on ethanol, the substance in wine and beer that causes drunkenness.
items.cn: 化学把这个词固定在乙醇上，即葡萄酒与啤酒中致醉的那种物质。

items.en: The word widened again to drinks in general and to the whole chemical class of alcohols.
items.cn: 这个词再度扩展，既泛指酒类，也指整个醇类化合物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on alcohol; the near-meaning group gathers the substance and the drinks in other words.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alcohol 构成的词；近义组收这种物质与酒类的其他说法。

entries.definition: Containing alcohol, or a person dependent on it.
entries.definitionCN: 含酒精的，或指对酒精依赖的人。

entries.definition: The illness of being unable to control one's drinking.
entries.definitionCN: 无法控制饮酒的疾病。

entries.definition: A related class of chemical compounds, named from alcohol and dehydrogenated.
entries.definitionCN: 一类相关化合物，名称由 alcohol 与「脱氢」缩合而成。

entries.definition: The precise chemical name for the alcohol in drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 酒类中所含酒精的精确化学名称。

entries.definition: Strong distilled drink such as whisky or gin.
entries.definitionCN: 威士忌、金酒之类的蒸馏烈酒。

entries.definition: Strong alcoholic drinks, in a formal or trade sense.
entries.definitionCN: 烈酒，多用于正式或行业语境。

normalIntro.en: Two real layers carry the word: Arabic al-kuhl, a fine powder, and the alchemists' use of it for distilled liquid.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实层次承载这个词：阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl 指细粉，以及炼金术士用它称呼蒸馏液。

normal.en: The al- at the start is the Arabic article, the same one as in algebra and alchemy.
normal.cn: 开头的 al- 是阿拉伯语冠词，与 algebra、alchemy 中的那个 al- 是同一个。

normal.en: The word travelled from eye make-up to distilled liquid to the drinks on the table.
normal.cn: 这个词从眼影走到蒸馏液，再走到餐桌上的酒。

normal.en: Chemists kept the name for the whole family, so methanol and sugar alcohols count too.
normal.cn: 化学家把名字留给了整个家族，所以甲醇与糖醇也算。

normal.en: Alcohol is uncountable for the substance and countable for the chemical compounds.
normal.cn: 指这种物质时不可数，指具体化合物时可数。

normal.en: Do not double the l: a-l-c-o-h-o-l.
normal.cn: 不要写双 l：a-l-c-o-h-o-l。

abstract.en: A word for cosmetics became a word for chemistry and then for a social problem, which is a long journey for one noun.
abstract.cn: 一个化妆品词变成化学词，又变成社会问题词，这对一个名词来说是很长的旅程。

abstract.en: The same substance is a solvent, a drink and a health risk, and the word refuses to separate them.
abstract.cn: 同一种物质既是溶剂、又是饮品、又是健康风险，而这个词拒绝把它们分开。

abstract.en: Naming the substance rather than the drink is a way of making a social habit sound clinical.
abstract.cn: 用物质而非饮品来命名，是一种让社交习惯听起来像临床问题的方式。

examples.en: The doctor asked how much alcohol he drank each week.
examples.cn: 医生问他每周喝多少酒。

examples.en: This cleaner contains alcohol and should not be used near a flame.
examples.cn: 这种清洁剂含酒精，不应在明火附近使用。

examples.en: Sugar alcohols are used as sweeteners in many processed foods.
examples.cn: 糖醇被用作许多加工食品的甜味剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱抠喝」——爱抠着瓶子喝的人，桌上少不了酒精。

root: 源自阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl「锑粉、精细提炼之物」，经中世纪拉丁语进入英语，先指粉末，后指蒸馏酒，最终固定为乙醇。

sensesIntro.en: One substance runs through all three senses: the chemical itself, the drinks built on it, and the whole family of related compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项贯穿着同一种物质：化学物质本身、以它为基础的饮品，以及整个相关的化合物家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass bottle of clear liquid with nothing on the label but a chemical formula.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着透明液体的玻璃瓶，标签上只有一行化学式。

branches.en: a swab of clear liquid on a laboratory bench
branches.cn: 实验台上的一小摊透明液体

branches.en: glasses filled at a dinner table
branches.cn: 餐桌上被斟满的杯子

branches.en: a bottle kept on the top shelf
branches.cn: 放在最上层架子上的那瓶酒

branches.en: a formula written on a whiteboard
branches.cn: 白板上写下的一条化学式

branches.en: one liquid, named by its chemistry and by its effects
branches.cn: 同一种液体，既按化学命名，也按效果命名

intro.cn: 阿拉伯语冠词与名词、它们的拉丁语与英语后裔，以及构成词族的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word entered Latin from Arabic as alcohol; it is not a native Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从阿拉伯语进入拉丁语作 alcohol，并非拉丁语本族词根。

definition_zh: 凹室；壁龛；（花园中的）凉亭
definition_en: a small recessed space in a room, or a sheltered place in a garden
core_image: 墙里挖出的一个小天地：三面有壁，一人一椅刚刚好
scene: 书房一侧的墙凹进去，摆着一张书桌，正好容得下一个人。He sat reading in the alcove by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 alcove 是「凹室」（第 1 个义项：墙体凹入形成的小空间）；句意是他坐在窗边的凹室里读书。

derivatives.zh: alcove 加 -ed 转作形容词（罕用），义为「带凹室的」
义近的姊妹词，源自法语，义为「壁龛；（喻）定位」

senses.title: A recessed space in a room
senses.definition: a small partly enclosed space formed by part of a wall set back
senses.definitionCN: 由墙面内凹形成、部分围合的小空间
senses.example: The bed fits neatly into an alcove in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 床正好嵌进墙上的凹室里。
senses.why: The Arabic word named a vaulted or arched recess, and English kept the picture of a space cut into a wall.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语原词指带拱顶的凹处，英语保留了「从墙体里切出一块空间」的画面。

senses.title: A sheltered spot in a garden
senses.definition: a small sheltered area outdoors, often shaded by trees or built as a bower
senses.definitionCN: 户外的遮蔽小境，常由树荫围合或筑成亭阁
senses.example: Vines shaded the garden alcove where they drank their coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 藤蔓给花园凉亭搭起荫凉，他们在那里喝咖啡。
senses.why: A sheltered outdoor nook works like an indoor recess, so the same word covers the bower among the trees.
senses.whyCN: 户外的避风小境功能上如同室内的凹龛，于是同一个词也覆盖了树间的亭阁。

intro.en: From Arabic for 'the vault', travelling through Spanish into English architecture.
intro.cn: 源自阿拉伯语「拱顶」，经西班牙语进入英语建筑词汇。

items.en: al-qubba meant the vault or dome, with the article al- attached.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qubba 意为「拱顶、穹顶」，al- 为定冠词。

items.en: Spanish alcoba kept the sense of a vaulted recess or bedroom alcove.
items.cn: 西班牙语 alcoba 保留「拱形凹室、卧室凹龛」之义。

items.en: French alcôve broadened the word to garden shelters as well.
items.cn: 法语 alcôve 把词义扩及花园凉亭。

items.en: English alcove entered in the 17th century, first for recesses in rooms.
items.cn: 17 世纪英语借入 alcove，最初指室内凹室。

items.en: Today it names any cozy recess, from bedrooms to breakfast nooks.
items.cn: 现代英语泛指一切舒适的凹入空间，从卧室龛到早餐角。

note.en: The first group gathers Arabic al- cousins and a sound-alike; the second gathers words for recessed spaces.
note.cn: 第一组收阿拉伯语 al- 同源词与音近词；第二组收表示「凹入空间」的词。

entries.definition: having an alcove or alcoves
entries.definitionCN: 带凹室的

entries.definition: a chemical substance; shares the Arabic article al-, otherwise unrelated in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 碱；同以阿拉伯语 al- 开头，语义无关

entries.definition: a puckered fabric; only vaguely similar in ending, unrelated root
entries.definitionCN: 纹凸织物；仅词尾略似，词源无关

entries.definition: a small sheltered corner, informal
entries.definitionCN: 小角落；隐蔽处，口语化

entries.definition: a space set back into a wall
entries.definitionCN: 壁凹；墙内凹进的空间

entries.definition: a recess, especially for a statue or ornament
entries.definitionCN: 壁龛；（喻）合适的定位

entries.definition: a shady, leafy shelter in a garden
entries.definitionCN: 树荫凉亭；幽居处，文学用法

entries.definition: a small partitioned space for one person
entries.definitionCN: 小隔间；单人隔开的格子间

normalIntro.en: al- is the Arabic article and -cove suggests a sheltered hollow, like a cove on a coast.
normalIntro.cn: al- 是阿拉伯语冠词，-cove 让人想起海湾的避风小湾：一个被围起来的小天地。

normal.en: al-qubba meant the vault; alcove keeps the arch.
normal.cn: al-qubba 意为拱顶，alcove 保留了拱形。

normal.en: Think of a bed set into the wall: an alcove bed.
normal.cn: 想想嵌进墙里的床：alcove bed。

normal.en: A breakfast alcove is a table tucked into a recess.
normal.cn: 早餐角就是把桌子塞进凹室的布置。

normal.en: Al- words from Arabic: alcove, alcohol, algebra.
normal.cn: 来自阿拉伯语的 al- 词：alcove、alcohol、algebra。

normal.en: Niche and nook are near neighbours of alcove.
normal.cn: niche 与 nook 是 alcove 的近邻词。

abstract.en: Picture a child hiding in a space the wardrobe leaves against the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子躲在衣柜与墙之间的小空间里。

abstract.en: See a lamp, a chair, and one reader inside three walls.
abstract.cn: 想象三面墙里的一盏灯、一把椅、一个读书人。

abstract.en: Imagine vines closing over a bench like green curtains.
abstract.cn: 想象藤蔓像绿帘一样罩住长凳。

examples.en: She carved a tiny alcove for her book collection.
examples.cn: 她为藏书凿出一个小小的壁龛。

examples.en: The apartment's sleeping alcove faces east.
examples.cn: 公寓的睡眠凹室朝东。

examples.en: They whispered together in a shadowy alcove of the hall.
examples.cn: 他们在大厅一个幽暗的凹室里低声交谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱靠屋」——爱人靠墙凹进去的小角落，一坐就是一下午。

root: 阿拉伯语 al-qubba「拱顶」（al- 为定冠词）经西班牙语 alcoba、法语 alcôve 于 17 世纪进入英语，由「拱形凹处」泛化为室内凹室与园中凉亭。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses move the same recessed nook outdoors: first cut into a wall, then roofed by leaves.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项把同一个凹入小境从室内搬到室外：先是嵌进墙里，再是覆于枝叶之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three walls and a lamp, a room inside a room.
core.cn: 核心意象：三面墙与一盏灯，房中之房。

branches.en: a bed fitted into the curve of a wall
branches.cn: 嵌进墙弯里的床

branches.en: a statue standing in a niche
branches.cn: 立于壁龛中的雕像

branches.en: coffee drunk under vine-shaded beams
branches.cn: 在藤蔓荫蔽的亭架下喝咖啡

branches.en: lovers finding a quiet corner of the garden
branches.cn: 恋人在花园寻得的僻静一角

branches.en: the same small shelter, built by mason or by leaves
branches.cn: 同一个小小的庇护所：或由砖石砌成，或由枝叶织就

intro.en: An Arabic article plus a root for vault, with Romance languages as carriers.
intro.cn: 阿拉伯语冠词加「拱顶」词根，由罗曼语诸语言接力传递。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root here; the line runs Arabic to Spanish and French.
latinIntro.cn: 此处无拉丁词根；传承线为阿拉伯语经西班牙语与法语。

definition_zh: 市议员；（英国部分城市的）高级市政官
definition_en: an elected member of a city council, or in Britain a senior civic official
core_image: 会议上年纪最长的那位老者：全城的老管家
scene: 市镇厅里挂着他祖父的画像，他刚刚在议事桌前坐下。The alderman cut the ribbon at the new library.
sceneCN: 这里 alderman 是「市议员」（第 1 个义项：市镇议会的成员）；句意是这位市议员为新图书馆剪彩。

derivatives.zh: alderman 加 -ic，义为「市议员的；与市政官职有关的」
alderman 加 -ship，义为「市议员职位（身分）」
同根基础词，义为「长者；长辈」，与 alder 同源

senses.title: A member of a city council
senses.definition: an elected or appointed member of the governing body of a city or borough
senses.definitionCN: 市政机构中经选举或任命产生的成员
senses.example: The alderman pushed the council to repave the old streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这位市议员推动议会重新铺设老街的路面。
senses.why: The word began as 'elder man': the older, experienced men who governed a town became its councillors.
senses.whyCN: 该词本义为「长者」：掌管城镇的年长有经验者，后来成为市议员。

senses.title: A senior civic official in Britain
senses.definition: in some British cities, a ceremonial or senior member of the council, historically elected for life
senses.definitionCN: 在英国部分城市，指议会中资深或礼典性成员，旧时为终身职
senses.example: The aldermen in their chain of office led the mayor's procession.
senses.exampleCN: 佩戴官链的高级市政官们走在市长队伍的最前面。
senses.why: When councils split into ordinary members and senior figures, the older title settled on the senior rank.
senses.whyCN: 当议会分出普通议员与资深成员两等，这个含「老」的古老头衔便落在资深一席上。

intro.en: An Old English title meaning simply 'older man', narrowed over centuries to a civic office.
intro.cn: 一个古英语头衔，本义只是「年长之人」，数百年来收窄为一项市政职务。

items.en: *aldiz meant old or grown, the root behind elder and old.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *aldiz 意为「年老的、成长的」，是 elder 与 old 的词根。

items.en: ealdorman meant a senior man, later a chief or governor of a shire.
items.cn: 古英语 ealdorman 意为「年长者」，后指郡的长官或首领。

items.en: The form shortened to alderman as the shire office faded and town government rose.
items.cn: 中古英语缩略为 alderman，郡职式微而城镇治理兴起。

items.en: The word settled on senior members of city councils, still ranked above ordinary councillors.
items.cn: 16 世纪该词专指市议会资深成员，地位高于普通议员。

items.en: In America it is an ordinary council member; in Britain the senior rank was abolished in the 1970s but survives in titles.
items.cn: 在美国指普通市议员；在英国，资深市政官职已于 20 世纪 70 年代废除，仅存于头衔之中。

note.en: The first group gathers the elder family; the second gathers civic titles and officials.
note.cn: 第一组收 elder 词族；第二组收市政头衔与官员称谓。

entries.definition: an older person, or one of longer standing in a community

entries.definition: polite word for old, of people

entries.definitionCN: （中世纪英格兰）地方长官

entries.definition: the elected head of a city government
entries.definitionCN: 市长

entries.definition: a respected senior figure in a community or church

normalIntro.en: The word is alder plus man: the older man who runs the town.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 alder（年长的）加 man：掌管镇子的长者。

normal.en: alder is an old form of elder.
normal.cn: alder 是 elder 的旧形。

normal.en: Old English ealdorman governed a shire.
normal.cn: 古英语 ealdorman 掌管一郡。

normal.en: In Chicago, each ward elects an alderman.
normal.cn: 在芝加哥，每个选区选出一名市议员。

normal.en: The plural is aldermen, like men for man.
normal.cn: 复数是 aldermen，如 man 变 men。

normal.en: British aldermen were the senior rank until the 1970s.
normal.cn: 英国的资深市政官职到 20 世纪 70 年代才废除。

abstract.en: Picture the oldest man at a town meeting, chair drawn to the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象镇民大会上最年长者把椅子拉到桌首。

abstract.en: See a heavy gold chain of office over a dark coat.
abstract.cn: 想象深色外套上挂着的沉重金色官链。

abstract.en: Imagine a man remembering every street of the town as it was fifty years ago.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人记得五十年前镇上每一条街的模样。

examples.en: The alderman campaigned on cleaner streets.
examples.cn: 这位市议员以整治街道为竞选纲领。

examples.en: Aldermen debated the bridge project late into the night.
examples.cn: 市政官们就桥梁工程辩论至深夜。

examples.en: His grandfather served as alderman for the riverside ward.
examples.cn: 他的祖父曾任滨河选区的市议员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥德曼」——奥！这位老德高望重的曼（人），管着全城大事。

root: 古英语 ealdorman「年长者；郡长官」由 eald「老的」（原始日耳曼语 *aldiz）加 man 构成，中古英语缩为 alderman；由「郡之长老」转为城镇议会资深成员，今指市议员。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one chair at the council table: an ordinary elected member, and the senior ceremonial figure above the rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项同坐议会一席：一是普通民选议员，二是高于众人的资深礼典性市政官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the town's oldest steward, chair at the head of the council table.
core.cn: 核心意象：全城的老管家，坐在议事桌的首席。

branches.en: a ward's chosen man arguing for new pavements
branches.cn: 选区选出的议员为新铺路力争

branches.en: cutting ribbons and hearing complaints door to door
branches.cn: 剪彩致辞、挨户倾听诉求

branches.en: a gold chain worn in the mayor's procession
branches.cn: 市长游行队伍中佩戴的金色官链

branches.cn: 老城镇里的终身荣誉席位

branches.en: the elder's chair, whether by vote or by seniority

intro.en: An old adjective for aged plus man, worn down by centuries of speech.
intro.cn: 古老的「年老」形容词加上 man，历经数百年口语磨损而成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element here; the whole word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 此处无拉丁成分；整词为日耳曼语源。

core_image: 退潮后的礁石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色薄膜，远处海带的长带随浪摆动
scene: 退潮后的礁石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色薄膜，浅水里还有成片的长带随浪摆动。At low tide the rocks are covered with a slippery brown-green film of algae, and longer ribbons sway in the shallows.
sceneCN: 这里 algae 指「附生在湿石与浅水中的藻类」（第 1 个义项：藻类总称，从单细胞到大型海藻）；句意：退潮时岩石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色藻膜，较长的带状藻体在浅水中摆动。图中可辨识物件：退潮后的礁石、褐绿色薄膜、浅水、随浪摆动的长带状藻体。

pos.zh: 藻类（拉丁复数，常作集合名词，指从单细胞到大型海藻的一大类光合生物）
藻（拉丁单数 alga 的复数形式，指一个或多个藻体）

derivatives.zh: 藻的；藻类的
